challenged_claim: A universal finite pointwise bound on the conditional density of three active spectral coordinates after conditioning on all complementary spectral coordinates follows from cap-one independent physical inputs.
counterexample: For iid Uniform[-1/2,1/2] physical inputs, use the normalized 4x4 Hadamard transform. With Q=Y1^2+Y2^2-Y3^2 the physical spectrum is {1,1,-1,0}. For Z=(X1+X2+X3+X4)/2 and z in [1/2,1], f_Z(z)=(8/3)(1-z)^3 while the joint (Y,Z) density is one on a rotated cube, so ||p_{Y|Z=z}||_infinity=3/[8(1-z)^3], which diverges as z approaches 1.
replacement: Keep unnormalized joint slice mass through the curved trace; f_Z(z)||p_{Y|Z=z}||_infinity=||p_{Y,Z}(.,z)||_infinity. This cancels the thin-slice normalization loss for the explicit source, but no universal raw integrated-fiber-sup theorem is asserted.
